Survival models in table_regression()

Source: R/table_regression_survival.R
table_regression_survival.Rd

table_regression() reads the Cox models of survival::coxph() and rms::cph(), the parametric accelerated failure time models of survival::survreg(), and the parametric models of flexsurv::flexsurvreg(). The coefficients fill the rows, as hazard ratios or time ratios under exponentiate = TRUE. For coxph and survreg fits, two families of columns give absolute effects: the difference in restricted mean survival time (RMST) over [0, tau] and the difference in cumulative incidence at at_time, by g-computation from the fitted model. The Cox model of a survey design, survey::svycoxph(), is described in table_regression_survey.

Usage

table_regression(
  models,
  tau = NULL,
  at_time = NULL,
  ...  # the arguments of every class: see ?table_regression
)

The other arguments are documented in table_regression(); the values they take for survival models are listed below.

Engines

ClassEngineAMEExponentiateBlocksvcov
coxphsurvival::coxph()RMST / risk diffHR-classical, CR0
survregsurvival::survreg()yes + RMST / risk diffTR (log-scale distributions)-classical, CR1
cphrms::cph()noHR-classical, CR0 (classical only without x = TRUE, y = TRUE)
flexsurvregflexsurv::flexsurvreg()noTR / HR (dist)distribution parametersclassical

AME: whether the average-marginal-effects columns are available; for coxph, the RMST and risk-difference columns stand in their place. Exponentiate: what exponentiate = TRUE gives. Blocks: the labeled blocks of rows the class adds below its coefficients. vcov: the values of vcov the class accepts. The same rows are returned by subset(table_regression_models(), family == "Survival").

The AME of a Cox model, coxph or cph, is refused: average marginal effects on a proportional-hazards fit are on an ambiguous survival or hazard scale, with unreliable standard errors. A flexsurvreg fit has no AME either: marginaleffects returns one row per time for it, not one effect per predictor. Neither cph nor flexsurvreg has the RMST and risk-difference columns, which are computed from a coxph or a survreg fit.

What the table shows

Coefficient rows. One row per coefficient, on the log-hazard scale for a Cox model and on the scale of the survival time (its log for the log-scale distributions) for survreg. Under exponentiate = TRUE, Cox models give hazard ratios and the log-scale distributions of survreg give time ratios. Identity-scale distributions are left untouched. The distribution parameters of a flexsurvreg fit render as a block of their own.

Absolute effects. The RMST difference and the risk difference are computed by g-computation (regression standardization): the survival curve of every subject is predicted under each level of the predictor, the other covariates kept as observed, the curves are averaged, and the two standardized curves are integrated up to tau (RMST) or read at at_time and complemented (risk). Their standard errors and intervals come from a nonparametric bootstrap of boot_n replicates. For coxph, the columns are defined for right-censored single-record fits. strata() is supported: standardization keeps each subject's own stratum baseline, and the note says so. For survreg, the closed-form curves of the AFT model are standardized directly.

Fit statistics. By default, n, the number of events and AIC for Cox fits; see Fit statistics below.

Arguments for this family

tau

The RMST horizon: the "rmst" columns report the restricted-mean-survival-time difference over [0, tau]. A positive time on the scale of the outcome, or "minmax" for the smallest per-group maximum follow-up; the note gives the value used. No default: the horizon defines the estimand. Supplied while no RMST column is requested, it is an error.

at_time

The landmark time of the "risk_diff" columns: the difference in cumulative incidence at at_time. A positive time on the scale of the outcome; no default. Supplied while no risk-difference column is requested, it is an error.

Column tokens of this family. These show_columns tokens are defined for coxph and survreg fits only:

  • "rmst", "rmst_se", "rmst_ci", "rmst_p": the RMST difference over [0, tau], its standard error, interval and p-value. They need tau.

  • "risk_diff", "risk_diff_se", "risk_diff_ci", "risk_diff_p": the difference in cumulative incidence at at_time. They need at_time.

  • "n_events": the event counts as events/N, per factor level and as model totals on continuous rows, for right-censored coxph fits (and binary outcomes outside this family).

The arguments shared with other classes take these values for survival models:

vcov, cluster

coxph and cph: "classical" and "CR0". survreg: "classical" and "CR1". flexsurvreg: "classical" only. See Standard errors, degrees of freedom and intervals.

boot_n

The number of bootstrap replicates of the RMST and risk-difference columns, 1000L by default.

exponentiate

Hazard ratios for Cox models, time ratios for the log-scale distributions of survreg. An exponentiated intercept is no ratio, and the note says what it estimates.

standardized

Refused: standardized coefficients are not defined for these classes.

show_fit_stats

"n_events" and "concordance" belong to the Cox models. See Fit statistics.

Standard errors, degrees of freedom and intervals

The coefficients are tested by Wald z. A robust vcov is the one cluster estimator of each class:

  • coxph: "CR0", the Lin-Wei grouped-dfbeta sandwich, the variance of coxph(cluster = ).

  • cph: "CR0", from rms::robcov(), which needs the fit's x = TRUE, y = TRUE.

  • survreg: "CR1", from sandwich::vcovCL(): the CR0 sandwich scaled by \(G/(G-1)\), G the number of clusters.

The Lin-Wei and robcov() sandwiches have no small-sample factor, hence "CR0"; the other CR* tokens are refused rather than mapped. For a censored coxph fit, cluster has one entry per subject.

Hierarchical comparison (nested = TRUE). Nested Cox fits, and nested survreg fits, are compared by likelihood-ratio test, c("lrt_change", "p_change"). Under "CR0" (coxph, cph) or "CR1" (survreg), and for survreg(robust = TRUE), the change test is the Wald chi-square of the added coefficients on the robust matrix. A Cox model without a coefficient (~ 1, or strata() alone) can be the first model of the hierarchy: its column shows the fit statistics, and the next model its likelihood-ratio test against it. Alone, it is refused, since it has no row to show. See Hierarchical (nested) model comparison in table_regression().

Fit statistics

Cox fits default to c("nobs", "n_events", "aic"): the number of events is reported beside n. survreg and flexsurvreg fits default to c("nobs", "aic"). On request:

  • "concordance": Harrell's C of a coxph fit, the value summary() reports. When the row is shown, the concordance leaves the note, which otherwise gives it with its standard error. cph fits have no concordance row or note.

  • "sigma": for survreg, the scale \(\sigma\) of the model, blank when strata give one scale per stratum. Asked for in a table where every survreg fit is stratified, it is refused. See Vocabulary tokens in table_regression().

Tied event times and the survival estimands

A Cox model has to decide what to do when several events share the same time, and survival::coxph() decides with ties = "efron" by default. The absolute estimands do not make a second decision: the baseline hazard behind the RMST-difference and risk-difference columns follows the tie-handling convention of the fit, as survival::survfit() and survival::basehaz() do. A ties = "breslow" fit gives a Breslow baseline; the default Efron fit gives an Efron baseline. The hazard-ratio column and the RMST column thus come from the same likelihood. To change the convention, change the fit.

The number of ties alone does not say whether the choice matters. What governs it is the fraction of tied events within the risk set, together with the effect size and the spread of the covariates: a large risk set dilutes a tied block, a small one (fine strata, matched or nested case-control designs) does not. A file with hundreds of tied days can be insensitive to the convention while a small stratified one with a handful of ties is not.

The approximations are all biased at finite sample size and agree asymptotically. Efron's has a much smaller small-sample bias (Hertz-Picciotto & Rockhill 1997), which makes it the default. Efron (1977), after Peto, expected the choice to make little difference in practice.

What is refused, and why

  • The AME columns for coxph and cph (see Engines), and for flexsurvreg.

  • The RMST and risk-difference columns for cph and flexsurvreg, for a coxph fit with time-transform tt() terms, and for a stratified survreg fit, whose per-stratum scale parameters are not standardized (refit without strata()).

  • "rmst" columns without tau, and "risk_diff" columns without at_time.

  • HC*, "bootstrap" and "jackknife" for every class, and the CR* tokens other than the one estimator of the class.

  • standardized for every class of this family.

References

Efron, B. (1977). The efficiency of Cox's likelihood function for censored data. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 72(359), 557-565.

Hertz-Picciotto, I. & Rockhill, B. (1997). Validity and efficiency of approximation methods for tied survival times in Cox regression. Biometrics, 53(3), 1151-1156.

See also

table_regression() for the arguments shared by all classes; table_regression_models() for the registry of supported classes and the other families; table_regression_survey for survey::svycoxph(); the Survival regression tables article.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(survival)
  lung$sex <- factor(lung$sex, labels = c("Male", "Female"))
  fit <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex, data = lung)
  print(table_regression(fit, exponentiate = TRUE))

  # RMST difference over the first year, from 200 bootstrap replicates.
  set.seed(1)
  print(table_regression(fit, show_columns = c("b", "rmst", "rmst_ci"),
                         tau = 365, boot_n = 200))
}
